subject: Clarify Order Form pricing bands, netting rules, and tax flow (MSA linkage)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Mar 2025 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Helio — initial commercial redlines and attachments

Kim / team,

Attaching Helio's v2 order form and the payment ladder they sent overnight. Key things they flagged in their cover note: pricing bands tied to usage thresholds, a request to net overage credits with minimum commit shortfalls (they called it "netting within the quarter"), and a question mark on tax/responsibility language (they expect reverse-charge in EU but want to confirm for US).

Files included: Helio_OrderForm_v2.docx, payment_ladder.xlsx (both attached).

Next asks from my side:
- Can legal provide a short list of high-risk redlines we should push back on before sending our redline?
- Finance (Jonas) — can you confirm whether we can accept netting at quarter level or if accounting needs month-by-month invoicing for ARR recognition?

I copied Lauren for legal triage. I propose we produce a single consolidated redline back to Helio by end of week.

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments (stubs): Helio_OrderForm_v2.docx (docx), payment_ladder.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@helio.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helio — initial commercial redlines and attachments

Thanks Ben — putting a pin in this and looping legal & finance. Emma, thanks for sending the OF and ladder; quick read-through below and a few asks so we can avoid multiple cycles.

Inline notes / asks for Helio: 
1) Pricing bands and the band-trigger language: we need the trigger to be based on billable usage reported per invoice period, not an "estimated monthly run-rate". Proposed: "Band determination will be based on actual billable usage as measured on the monthly invoice and reconciled each quarter." Please confirm.

2) Netting / overage credit vs. minimum commit: your draft suggests Helio can offset shortfalls against overage credits across the quarter. We can accept netting at quarter level if both parties agree to a single reconciliation invoice per quarter and that such netting does not change revenue recognition for Redwood. Proposed wrapper language that preserves revenue recognition: "Parties may mutually agree to reconcile and net amounts due for the applicable calendar quarter in a single reconciliation invoice; Redwood's revenue recognition will follow GAAP and is not altered by such netting."

3) Net terms & invoicing cadence: your current asks imply net45. Our standard is net30; if Helio requires net45 we need to know whether their procurement team will sign PO terms that reference net45. Can we agree to net30 for the order form and revisit with procurement if needed?

4) Taxes / reverse charge: we need Helio to confirm which entity is the payer (Helio U.S. or Helio EU); if EU entity uses reverse charge, please supply the VAT registration and the country-specific tax matrix. If Helio expects Redwood to gross up, call that out explicitly.

5) MSA linkage: please confirm that Exhibit B pricing in the MSA continues to govern pricing mechanics. If Helio intends the OF to supplant Exhibit B language, mark up the OF to make that explicit.

I've attached a quick redline with comments where the language should be tightened up: RDW_redline_helio_orderform.docx (redline stub). Lauren — would you please prioritize a brief legal memo on the high-risk clauses (points 1–4 above)? Jonas — can you flag anything in the payment ladder that would block quarter-level netting from an accounting perspective?

Emma, if you can provide the tax matrix and the entity that will be invoiced, we can produce a clean redline. If Helio prefers a short call to walk through the commercial constructs, Ben can coordinate.

Best,
Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments (stub): RDW_redline_helio_orderform.docx (redline)

From: Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@helio.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Mar 2025 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helio — initial commercial redlines and attachments

Kimberly / team,

Thanks for the quick read and the suggested language. A few quick clarifications from Helio: 
- We confirm Helio US will be the contracting entity for the first year. If we expand to EU entities later, we expect to use reverse-charge where applicable; attached is our current tax matrix for your review (Helio_tax_matrix.pdf).
- On netting: the procurement team prefers quarter-level reconciliation to reduce admin burden; they are comfortable with a single reconciliation invoice per quarter if Redwood agrees. They explicitly do NOT want netting to obscure invoice-level remittances (i.e., we still need line-item detail).
- Net terms: procurement will accept net30 if Helio legal and procurement can route payment approvals more quickly; we will advise, but trying to avoid a hard requirement for net45.

On the MSA linkage: Helio's intent was not to supplant Exhibit B — just to ensure the OF references Exhibit B and that the payment ladder becomes an attached exhibit to the OF. We will mark the OF to reference Exhibit B and include the ladder as Exhibit A to the OF.

We reviewed your redline (Kim). We have a couple of counter-suggestions in places where you asked for fixed "monthly invoice" triggers. Helio proposes: "Band determination will be based on reported billable usage for the applicable month, reconciled at quarter-end for band assignment and pricing." That preserves monthly-cycle reporting but allows quarter-end band assignment.

If that language is acceptable to Redwood, we can update the OF and re-send. Attaching Helio_tax_matrix.pdf.

--
Emma Ruiz
Contracts Manager | Helio Labs
emma.ruiz@helio.com

Attachments (stub): Helio_tax_matrix.pdf (pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Mar 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helio — initial commercial redlines and attachments — finance notes

Thanks — quick finance/ops callout after reviewing the ladder and the proposed quarter-level netting: 

1) Quarter-level netting is acceptable from an AR workflow standpoint, provided Helio agrees to a single reconciliation invoice with line-item detail and a short SLA for disputes (we typically ask 30 days post-reconciliation). Please capture that in the OF.

2) For revenue recognition we need the invoice recognition date to be tied to the invoice issuance for the reconciliation (i.e., we cannot backdate recognition). Our suggested clause: "Reconciliation invoice issued by Redwood for the applicable quarter will be issued within 15 calendar days following quarter close; disputes must be raised within 30 days of receipt. Revenue recognition follows invoice issuance dates."

3) Net terms: Jonas confirms we can remain on net30 for the OF. If Helio procurement returns a PO with net45, we will escalate but accept net30 in the signed OF for start.

4) Taxes: the tax matrix Helio sent looks complete for now. We'll request final VAT proof if Helio pulls in an EU entity later.

Next steps I recommend: 
- Kimberly / Lauren to finalize the redline with the quarter-reconciliation language and the invoice/dispute SLA. 
- Ben to propose a 30-minute call with Helio procurement + contracts to confirm net30 and the ladder attachment approach (Ben: can you run availability?). 

I'll attach the final pricing table export I used for review (final_pricing_table.csv).

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
